::: {.why}
Choosing a fraction is choosing a drawdown distribution, and stating it that way makes the decision concrete instead of a matter of temperament.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Map the Kelly fraction to the distribution of maximum drawdown over a year, and report the mapping for your own strategy.
- State the fraction you will run and the drawdown you are accepting by choosing it.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Build the mapping: simulate one year of your strategy at Kelly fractions from 0.1 to 1.5 and report median and 95th percentile maximum drawdown for each. Plot both against the fraction. The 95th percentile curve is the one to make the decision on.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Add the growth cost: on the same axes, plot expected log growth against fraction. Half Kelly gives three quarters of the growth at much less than half the drawdown, and that asymmetry is the whole argument. Confirm the ratio on your own numbers rather than quoting it.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write down your chosen fraction and the 95th percentile drawdown it implies, as a commitment in the milestone report.
:::
:::
